# Feasibility of two requested course periods

A planner can save a solver call if it can certify that two requested course placements violate prerequisites or capacity. Evaluate the odd-numbered CSPLib 030 MiniZinc instances for development. Leave all even-numbered instances out of scoring. Use every administrative limit in the archive as written. The endpoint is feasibility under those limits. The archive's distinct load-minimization objective and the P10 teacher-correction endpoint are outside this experiment.

For each instance generate 16 distinct two-course requests with uniformly drawn periods and 16 with periods drawn from each course's original precedence window. Sample courses uniformly without replacement per request. Use the instance number as the Python RNG seed. Record structurally impossible base instances separately. After applying both requests, propagate precedence bounds. For each contiguous term interval, compare compulsory and possible course counts and credits to the published upper and lower limits. Return an infeasibility certificate on a contradiction, otherwise defer to an exact solver.

Compare full interval checks with precedence alone, singleton capacity checks plus precedence, and an exact CP-SAT feasibility model used for every request. The oracle sees original rules and both requests without manually reduced domains. Independently validate every returned timetable. Retain censored solves and unexpected disagreements. The submitted request distribution is simulated. Include the number of exact calls each safe filter can avoid. A development improvement requires at least five percentage points more calls saved than each simpler filter and no contradicted certificates. Solves have one worker and a deterministic limit of 3 units per request. A reduction in solver calls cannot establish latency or teacher editing benefit.
